title: Nationalist Response in the Wake of World War II
desc: Congress crisis over Bose's presidency (Haripura, Tripuri), Gandhi-Bose ideological differences, Congress ministries' resignation, Wardha CWC debates, Lahore/Pakistan Resolution, August Offer, Individual Satyagraha, and the Cripps Mission

questions.q: What was the primary source of internal disarray within the Congress in the aftermath of the Civil Disobedience Movement, as perceived by Gandhi?
o: Rising corruption, indiscipline, rivalries among leaders, and issues of bogus membership
A complete lack of funds to run the organisation
Disagreement over whether to support the British monarchy
The refusal of provincial governments to cooperate with the Congress
questions.e: Gandhi perceived rising corruption and indiscipline, petty rivalries among leaders, and issues of bogus membership and unethical means used to control Congress committees.

questions.q: At the Haripura Congress session (February 1938), Subhash Chandra Bose, as president, was instrumental in setting up which body for the country's economic development?
o: The National Planning Committee
The Reserve Bank of India
The Planning Commission of independent India
The Indian Statistical Institute
questions.e: At Haripura, Bose spoke of economic development through planning and was instrumental in setting up the National Planning Committee.

questions.q: Regarding the 1939 Congress presidential election, which of the following is correct?
o: Subhash Bose defeated Gandhi's preferred candidate Pattabhi Sitaramayya by 1580 votes to 1377, with support from the Congress Socialist Party and communists
Pattabhi Sitaramayya defeated Bose decisively with an overwhelming majority
The election was cancelled due to procedural irregularities
Nehru contested and won the presidency unopposed
questions.e: Bose won by 1580 votes against 1377, defeating Gandhi-backed Pattabhi Sitaramayya, with support from the Congress Socialist Party and the communists; Gandhi called it his own defeat.

questions.q: At the Tripuri Congress session (March 1939), Bose's presidential address proposed which course of action regarding Britain?
o: A six-month ultimatum to Britain demanding independence, failing which a mass civil disobedience movement should be launched
Immediate unconditional support for Britain's war preparations
A referendum among princely states on joining the Congress
Permanent boycott of all future Congress sessions
questions.e: Bose proposed giving Britain a six-month ultimatum to grant independence, with mass civil disobedience to follow if rejected, believing international crisis offered strategic advantage.

questions.q: At Tripuri, the resolution moved by Govind Ballabh Pant asked Bose to:
o: Nominate the working committee in accordance with the wishes of Gandhiji
Resign immediately from the Congress presidency
Merge the Congress with the Muslim League
Postpone all further Congress sessions indefinitely
questions.e: Pant's resolution, passed without opposition even from socialists and communists, reaffirmed faith in Gandhian policies and asked Bose to nominate a working committee per Gandhi's wishes.

questions.q: Why did Bose ultimately resign from the Congress presidency in April 1939, despite winning the election?
o: He refused to nominate a new working committee acceptable to Gandhi and could not bridge the ideological gap with Gandhi, who threatened to withdraw from leadership otherwise
He was expelled by a unanimous vote of the AICC
He voluntarily stepped down to contest provincial elections instead
The British government banned him from holding the post
questions.e: Bose refused to nominate a working committee in line with Gandhi's wishes; with Gandhi unwilling to compromise and most Congress leaders preferring unity under Gandhi, Bose saw no option but to resign.

questions.q: Following his resignation, what disciplinary action did the Congress Working Committee take against Bose in August 1939?
o: He was removed as president of the Bengal Provincial Congress Committee and debarred from holding elective Congress office for three years
He was permanently expelled from the Congress party
He was arrested and imprisoned by the British government
He was stripped of his Indian citizenship
questions.e: After Bose called for an all-India protest against an AICC resolution, the CWC removed him from the Bengal PCC presidency and barred him from elective office for three years.

questions.q: Who was elected Congress president after Bose's resignation in 1939, resolving the immediate crisis?
o: Rajendra Prasad
Jawaharlal Nehru
Maulana Abul Kalam Azad
Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel
questions.e: Rajendra Prasad was elected Congress president following Bose's resignation in April 1939.

questions.q: In May 1939, Bose and his followers formed which new party within the Congress?
o: The Forward Bloc
The Congress Socialist Party
The Kisan Sabha
The Swaraj Party
questions.e: Bose and his followers formed the Forward Bloc in May 1939 (at Makur, Unnao) as a new party within the Congress.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements on Gandhi's and Bose's respective views on the appropriate means of struggle:
1. Gandhi believed non-violence was necessary because an unarmed mass had little chance in armed rebellion.
2. Bose viewed civil disobedience as effective only if accompanied by a movement prepared to use violence if necessary.
3. Both agreed that any means, however violent, were justified if the end was national independence.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
o: 1 and 2 only
1 only
2 and 3 only
1, 2 and 3
questions.e: Statements 1 and 2 accurately reflect the two leaders' positions. Statement 3 is incorrect: Gandhi explicitly rejected the idea that any means could justify an end, insisting that means and ends must both be good.

questions.q: Regarding Bose's views on the appropriate form of government for India, which of the following is correct?
o: He initially favoured democracy but later argued that an authoritarian state would be necessary, at least initially, to implement socialist economic reforms
He consistently advocated for a purely democratic system throughout his political career with no variation
He believed India should remain under British dominion status permanently
He rejected socialism entirely in favour of unregulated capitalism
questions.e: Bose came to believe that democracy alone could not push through socialist economic reforms, arguing (e.g., at Tokyo University, 1944) for an authoritarian state, at least in the initial phase of nation-building.

questions.q: On October 21, 1943, Bose proclaimed the formation of which body, in which he held multiple top posts including head of state, prime minister, and minister for war and foreign affairs?
o: The Provisional Government of Azad Hind (Free India)
The Indian National Congress Working Committee
The All India Forward Bloc Council
The Indian Constituent Assembly
questions.e: Bose proclaimed the Provisional Government of Azad Hind (Free India) on October 21, 1943, retaining for himself the positions of Supreme Commander of the INA, head of state, prime minister, and minister for war and foreign affairs.

questions.q: Bose termed his ideological synthesis of Socialism and Fascism-style discipline and efficiency by which name?
o: Samyavada
Sarvodaya
Ramrajya
Swadeshi
questions.e: As early as 1930, Bose called for a synthesis of Socialism's justice and equality with Fascism's discipline and efficiency, terming this synthesis 'samyavada'.

questions.q: Which of the following best characterises Bose's relationship with Fascist and Nazi ideology?
o: He admired their discipline and orderliness but rejected racial superiority theories and Fascist support for capitalism, viewing his alliance with the Axis as a pragmatic revolutionary strategy
He was an ideological Nazi who fully endorsed Hitler's racial theories
He had no interaction with or knowledge of Fascist or Nazi Germany at all
He supported Fascism only because he agreed with its capitalist economic model
questions.e: Bose disapproved of Nazi racialism and suppression of democratic institutions but admired their discipline; his supporters argue his association with Germany and Japan was dictated by revolutionary strategy, not ideological kinship.

questions.q: Regarding Gandhi's Ramrajya as outlined in Hind Swaraj (1909), which of the following is correct?
o: It envisioned a stateless society of self-sufficient, decentralised village republics with panchayats as the basic unit of self-governance
It called for a strong centralised state with a large standing army for national defence
It advocated rapid industrialisation modelled on the Soviet Union
It proposed direct British-style parliamentary democracy for India
questions.e: Gandhi's Ramrajya envisioned decentralised, self-sufficient village republics governed by panchayats, with minimal state power; Judith Brown observed that Gandhi could 'properly be called an anarchist'.

questions.q: On the subject of religion, which of the following distinguishes Bose's approach from Gandhi's?
o: Bose, though personally inspired by Hindu spirituality and the Bhagavad Gita, insisted Free India's state must remain neutral and treat religion as a private matter, while Gandhi could not conceive of a state entirely without religion
Bose was an avowed atheist who rejected all religious symbolism in politics, unlike the deeply religious Gandhi
Gandhi insisted the state must actively promote a single religion, while Bose opposed any religious content in politics
Both leaders held identical views advocating a theocratic state
questions.e: Bose, inspired by Hindu spirituality yet a committed secularist, wanted Free India's state to be neutral on religion as a private matter, whereas Gandhi's vision of the state was itself grounded in religious and moral principles.

questions.q: Which women's regiment did Bose form within the Indian National Army in 1943, commanded by Captain Lakshmi Swaminathan?
o: The Rani of Jhansi Regiment
The Durga Vahini
The Bharat Mahila Sena
The Azad Hind Mahila Dal
questions.e: Bose formed the Rani of Jhansi Regiment in the INA in 1943, commanded by Captain Lakshmi Swaminathan (later Sahgal), training women as soldiers rather than only in support roles.

questions.q: Regarding views on women, which of the following is correct?
o: Gandhi, while championing women's emancipation from social ills and purdah, still held a comparatively traditionalist view of gendered domestic roles, whereas Bose considered women full equals fit for combat and public life
Gandhi believed women should have no role in the freedom struggle at all
Bose opposed involving women in the INA in any capacity
Both leaders held identical views with no difference on gender roles
questions.e: Gandhi opposed child marriage, dowry, and purdah and brought women into the freedom struggle, yet retained traditionalist views of women's domestic 'dharma'; Bose considered women equals fit even for combat duty in the INA.

questions.q: On the outbreak of the Second World War, which of the following statements is correct regarding India's involvement?
o: The British Government of India declared India's support for the war on September 3, 1939, without consulting Indian political opinion
The Congress was formally consulted and gave its consent before India was drawn into the war
India was granted immediate independence in exchange for war support
The princely states alone decided India's participation in the war
questions.e: On September 3, 1939, following Britain's declaration of war against Germany, the British Government of India unilaterally declared India's support for the war effort without consulting Indian opinion.

questions.q: What were the two basic conditions of the Congress's conditional offer to cooperate in the war effort, made to Viceroy Linlithgow?
o: A constituent assembly to determine India's post-war political structure, and immediate establishment of a genuinely responsible government at the Centre
Complete transfer of the army to Indian command and abolition of the Governor-General's post
Release of all political prisoners and a ban on the Muslim League
Formation of a coalition government exclusively with the Muslim League
questions.e: The Congress conditionally offered wartime cooperation on the basis that (i) a constituent assembly be convened after the war to determine India's political structure, and (ii) a genuinely responsible government be set up immediately at the Centre.

questions.q: At the Wardha CWC meeting on the question of India's support to Britain's war effort, which of the following correctly matches the leader with their position?
o: Gandhi favoured unconditional support to the Allies; Bose and other socialists favoured no support to either side and immediate civil disobedience; Nehru favoured no Indian participation without freedom but also opposed exploiting Britain's difficulty
Gandhi, Bose and Nehru all held an identical position of unconditional support to Britain
Gandhi favoured immediate civil disobedience while Bose favoured unconditional support to Britain
Nehru alone supported the war while Gandhi and Bose opposed all cooperation
questions.e: Gandhi wanted unconditional support to the Allies due to his opposition to Fascism; Bose and socialists like Narendra Dev and JP Narayan saw the war as an imperialist conflict on both sides and favoured immediate civil disobedience; Nehru favoured neither side but also opposed exploiting Britain's wartime difficulty. Gandhi ultimately went with Nehru's position.

questions.q: The CWC resolution adopted at Wardha (September 1939) on the war stated that:
o: India could not be party to a war fought for democratic freedom while that freedom was denied to India itself, and the government should declare its war aims and how democracy would be applied to India after the war
India would unconditionally support the war under all circumstances
Civil disobedience would be launched immediately regardless of the government's response
The princely states would be excluded from any future constitutional arrangement
questions.e: The CWC resolution condemned Fascist aggression but held that India could not support a war for democratic freedom while denied that freedom itself, demanding a declaration of British war aims and clarity on democracy's post-war application to India.

questions.q: In his statement of October 17, 1939, what did Viceroy Linlithgow propose?
o: Consultation with representatives of communities, parties and princes on modifying the Act of 1935, and setting up an advisory 'consultative committee', without defining British war aims beyond resisting aggression
Immediate grant of dominion status to India
Full transfer of defence and finance portfolios to Indians
Unconditional acceptance of the Congress's demand for a constituent assembly
questions.e: Linlithgow refused to define British war aims beyond 'resisting aggression', proposed consulting various interests on modifying the 1935 Act, and offered to set up a purely advisory consultative committee.

questions.q: According to the chapter, what was the British government's hidden agenda behind Linlithgow's October 1939 statement?
o: To provoke the Congress into confrontation, then use the resulting situation to acquire draconian powers and paint the Congress as pro-Axis to win international sympathy
To immediately grant India full independence after consulting all parties
To dissolve the Muslim League and support the Congress exclusively
To transfer all administrative powers to the princely states
questions.e: British policy aimed to provoke Congress confrontation to justify draconian powers (including a secret Draft Revolutionary Movement Ordinance) and to portray an aggressive Congress as pro-Japan/pro-Germany to win international sympathy.

questions.q: Following Linlithgow's October 1939 statement, on what date did the CWC decide to call upon Congress ministries to resign?
o: October 23, 1939
September 3, 1939
January 1940
August 1940
questions.e: On October 23, 1939, the CWC rejected the viceregal statement, decided not to support the war, and called upon Congress ministries in the provinces to resign.

questions.q:
Which of the following reasons did Gandhi and his supporters cite against launching an immediate mass struggle after Linlithgow's October 1939 statement?
1. They believed the Allied cause was just.
2. Communal sensitiveness and lack of Hindu-Muslim unity could cause riots.
3. The Congress organisation itself was in disarray.
4. The masses were not yet ready for a struggle.
How many of the above are correctly listed as reasons?
o: All four
Only three
Only two
Only one
questions.e: All four reasons — belief in the just Allied cause, fear of communal riots, disorganised Congress machinery, and unready masses — were cited by Gandhi and supporters against an immediate mass struggle.

questions.q: The Muslim League's Lahore Resolution (March 1940), popularly called the 'Pakistan Resolution', called for:
o: Grouping geographically contiguous Muslim-majority areas of the North-West and East into independent states with autonomous and sovereign constituent units
A single unified Indian state with proportional representation for all religions
Complete integration of princely states into British India
Abolition of separate electorates for Muslims
questions.e: The Lahore Resolution called for grouping contiguous Muslim-majority areas in the North-West and East into independent, sovereign states — the foundational demand later associated with Pakistan.

questions.q: At the Ramgarh session of the Congress (March 1940), presided over by Maulana Abul Kalam Azad, what was decided?
o: To leave the form and timing of the struggle to Gandhi, while declaring that Indians would accept nothing short of complete independence
To accept dominion status as a final settlement
To merge with the Muslim League on a joint platform
To indefinitely suspend all Congress political activity
questions.e: At Ramgarh, it was decided to leave the form and timing of any battle to Gandhi, while the Congress declared that Indians would accept nothing short of complete independence, not dominion status.

questions.q:
Which of the following provisions were included in the British government's August Offer (August 1940)?
1. Dominion status as the objective for India.
2. Expansion of the Viceroy's executive council with an Indian majority.
3. Setting up a constituent assembly after the war mainly composed of Indians.
4. No future constitution without the consent of minorities.
How many of the above are correctly listed as part of the August Offer?
o: All four
Only three
Only two
Only one
questions.e: All four elements — dominion status as the objective, an expanded executive council with Indian majority, a post-war constituent assembly, and a minority-consent clause — were part of the August Offer.

questions.q: How did the Congress and the Muslim League respectively respond to the August Offer (1940)?
o: The Congress rejected it, with Nehru declaring dominion status 'dead as a doornail', while the Muslim League welcomed the minority veto assurance and reiterated its demand for partition
Both the Congress and the Muslim League accepted the offer unconditionally
The Congress accepted it while the Muslim League rejected it outright
Both parties rejected the offer and jointly demanded immediate full independence
questions.e: Nehru dismissed dominion status as 'dead as a doornail' and the Congress rejected the offer; the Muslim League, however, welcomed the minority veto assurance and reaffirmed that partition was the only solution.

questions.q: Regarding the composition of the enlarged Viceroy's executive council in July 1941, which of the following is correct?
o: Indians were given a majority of 8 out of 12 seats for the first time, though the British retained control of defence, finance and home portfolios
Indians held all 12 seats with no British representation
The council was abolished entirely in favour of a fully elected legislature
Only princely state representatives were appointed to the council
questions.e: In July 1941, the executive council was enlarged to give Indians a majority of 8 out of 12 seats for the first time, though the British retained charge of defence, finance and home.

questions.q:
What were the stated aims of Gandhi's Individual Satyagraha launched in late 1940?
1. To show that nationalist patience was not due to weakness.
2. To express that Indians made no distinction between Nazism and colonial autocracy.
3. To give the government another opportunity to accept Congress demands peacefully.
4. To immediately overthrow British rule through mass armed rebellion.
How many of the above are correctly listed as aims?
o: Only three
All four
Only two
Only one
questions.e: Statements 1, 2 and 3 correctly describe the aims of Individual Satyagraha; it was explicitly a limited, non-violent movement, not an armed rebellion (statement 4 is incorrect).

questions.q: Who offered Individual Satyagraha first, and who was the second satyagrahi, according to Gandhi's plan?
o: Vinoba Bhave was the first, followed by Jawaharlal Nehru
Jawaharlal Nehru was the first, followed by Sardar Patel
Rajendra Prasad was the first, followed by Maulana Azad
Subhash Bose was the first, followed by Gandhi himself
questions.e: Vinoba Bhave was selected as the first individual satyagrahi, and Jawaharlal Nehru was the second; by May 1941, about 25,000 people had been convicted for individual civil disobedience.

questions.q: The movement in which satyagrahis would progressively march towards the capital after repeated arrests came to be known as:
o: The Delhi Chalo Movement
The Quit India Movement
The Dandi March
The Non-Cooperation Movement
questions.e: If the government did not arrest a satyagrahi, they would move into villages and eventually march towards Delhi — a movement known as the 'Delhi Chalo Movement'.

questions.q: Gandhi designated which leader as his chosen political successor, around the time of the CWC's late-1941 resolution offering conditional cooperation in India's defence?
o: Jawaharlal Nehru
Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel
Maulana Abul Kalam Azad
Subhash Chandra Bose
questions.e: Around this period, Gandhi designated Jawaharlal Nehru as his chosen successor, valuing Nehru's inclusive, all-India appeal over more sectionally-associated leaders like Patel, Rajaji, or Azad.

questions.q: According to Rajmohan Gandhi's account, why did Gandhi prefer Nehru over alternatives like Patel, Rajaji, Azad, or Kripalani as his successor?
o: Nehru most reliably reflected the pluralist, inclusive idea of India — trusted by Muslims despite being Hindu, respected across regions, and seen as a genuinely all-India leader
Nehru was the only candidate with prior administrative experience
Nehru was chosen purely because of seniority within the party
The other candidates had all resigned from active politics by this time
questions.e: Rajmohan Gandhi notes that unlike the more sectionally-associated alternatives, Nehru was trusted across religious and regional lines and embodied Gandhi's own pluralist, inclusive vision of India.

questions.q:
Why was the Cripps Mission sent to India in March 1942?
1. The Japanese threat to invade India had become real after British reverses in South-East Asia.
2. Allied powers (USA, USSR, China) pressured Britain to seek Indian cooperation.
3. Indian nationalists had signalled support for the Allied cause if power was transferred and independence promised after the war.
4. Britain wanted to formally grant India complete independence immediately.
How many of the above are correctly listed as reasons for the mission?
o: Only three
All four
Only two
Only one
questions.e: Statements 1, 2 and 3 are correct reasons; statement 4 is false — the Cripps Mission did not offer immediate complete independence, only a future dominion status arrangement.

questions.q: Which of the following was NOT among the main proposals of the Cripps Mission (March 1942)?
o: Immediate transfer of defence and control of the Indian army to an Indian-led government
Setting up of an Indian Union with dominion status, free to leave the Commonwealth
A post-war constituent assembly to frame a new constitution, elected by provincial assemblies and partly nominated by princes
The option for any unwilling province to have a separate constitution and form a separate Union
questions.e: The Cripps proposals kept defence of India in British hands during the war and retained the Governor-General's full powers; immediate transfer of defence control was not offered, unlike the other three listed proposals.

questions.q: How did the Cripps proposals differ from the earlier August Offer in terms of constitution-making?
o: Making of the constitution was now to be solely in Indian hands (not merely 'mainly' in Indian hands), with a concrete plan provided for the constituent assembly
The Cripps proposals removed all mention of a constituent assembly altogether
The August Offer had already granted full Indian control over constitution-making
There was no difference between the two offers on this point
questions.e: Unlike the August Offer, where the constitution-making body was 'mainly' Indian, the Cripps proposals made it solely Indian, with a concrete plan for a constituent assembly elected by provincial assemblies and partly nominated by princes.

questions.q:
Which of the following did the Congress object to in the Cripps proposals?
1. Offer of dominion status instead of complete independence.
2. Representation of princely states by nominees rather than elected representatives.
3. The right of provinces to secede from the Union.
4. Absence of any immediate transfer of power or real share in defence.
How many of the above are correctly listed as Congress objections?
o: All four
Only three
Only two
Only one
questions.e: The Congress objected to all four points: dominion status instead of independence, non-elected princely representation, the provincial secession clause undermining unity, and the lack of immediate power transfer or defence share.

questions.q: Which of the following did the Muslim League object to regarding the Cripps proposals?
o: The idea of a single Indian Union, the machinery for creating the constituent assembly, and the perceived denial of Muslims' right to self-determination and Pakistan
The proposal's failure to mention dominion status at all
The retention of the Governor-General's powers, which the League strongly supported removing
The absence of any provision for provincial secession, which the League wanted removed entirely
questions.e: The Muslim League objected to the single-Union framework, the constituent assembly's composition procedure, and felt the proposals denied Muslims the right to self-determination and creation of Pakistan.

questions.q: Who famously described the Cripps offer as 'a post-dated cheque'?
o: Mahatma Gandhi
Jawaharlal Nehru
Maulana Abul Kalam Azad
Subhash Chandra Bose
questions.e: Gandhi described the Cripps scheme as 'a post-dated cheque' on a failing bank, reflecting Congress's scepticism about British follow-through on the proposals.

questions.q: Which British officials are cited in the chapter as having consistently undermined Cripps' negotiating efforts?
o: Churchill, Amery, Linlithgow, and Ward (the commander-in-chief)
Stafford Cripps himself, who sabotaged his own mission deliberately
Mountbatten and Wavell, both serving as Viceroy at the time
Roosevelt and Chiang Kai-shek, who opposed Indian independence
questions.e: Churchill (Prime Minister), Amery (Secretary of State), Linlithgow (Viceroy), and Ward (Commander-in-Chief) are cited as consistently torpedoing Cripps' efforts, particularly over the question of the Viceroy's veto.

questions.q: Winston Churchill's remark, "I have not become His Majesty's first Minister to preside over the liquidation of the British Empire," reflects which broader dynamic described in the chapter?
o: British reluctance, especially at the highest levels, to genuinely concede self-government to India despite wartime pressures
Churchill's personal support for immediate Indian independence
A joint British-Congress consensus on maintaining the empire
Churchill's endorsement of the Cripps Mission's proposals in full
questions.e: Churchill's remark exemplifies the underlying British reluctance to loosen imperial control over India, consistent with the mission's ultimate failure due to rigid British attitudes.

questions.q:
According to the chapter's summary of the sequence of events, which of the following correctly orders these developments?
1. August Offer
2. Individual Satyagraha begins
3. Lahore (Pakistan) Resolution
4. Cripps Mission
Arrange in correct chronological order.
questions.e: Correct order: Lahore/Pakistan Resolution (March 1940) → August Offer (August 1940) → Individual Satyagraha begins (October 1940) → Cripps Mission (March 1942).
